title: Freelance: Client Default on ₹35,000 Approved Design Deliverable
input_narrative: I completed a freelance UI/UX redesign project for BrandVibe Marketing on 5 September 2024. All Figma assets and design system were approved via email on 10 September. I raised Invoice #BV-042 for Rs 35,000 payable within 15 days. They have used my designs in their live production web app, but have not paid the invoice. Now the founder is ignoring emails and blocked me on LinkedIn.

legal_assessment.summary_verdict: Failure to clear invoices for completed work constitutes breach of contract under Section 73 of the Indian Contract Act. If registered under MSME, you are entitled to 3x RBI bank rate compound interest.

applicable_statutes.official_title: Compensation for Loss or Damage Caused by Breach of Contract
applicable_statutes.plain_meaning: When a contract is broken, the party who suffers is entitled to receive compensation for any loss or damage naturally arising from the breach.
applicable_statutes.maximum_penalty_or_relief: Full recovery of dues plus consequential damages and interest.

applicable_statutes.act_name: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006
applicable_statutes.official_title: Mandatory Payment Period and Compound Interest for Delay
applicable_statutes.plain_meaning: Buyer must make payment within 45 days. Delayed payment attracts compound interest with monthly rests at 3 times the Bank Rate notified by RBI.
applicable_statutes.maximum_penalty_or_relief: Mandatory 3x RBI interest rate via MSME Samadhaan conciliation.

applicable_statutes.official_title: Statutory Period of Limitation for Recovery
applicable_statutes.plain_meaning: General civil recovery suits must be filed within 3 years from the date payment became due. Consumer complaints have a 2-year limitation (Section 69 CPA).
applicable_statutes.maximum_penalty_or_relief: Bar on judicial remedy if suit is not filed within the limitation period.

action_roadmap: Step 1: Issue the Formal Statutory Demand Notice demanding invoice clearance plus commercial interest within 15 days.
Step 2: If registered as MSME/Udyam, file an instant online recovery petition on the MSME Samadhaan portal (samadhaan.msme.gov.in).
Step 3: Initiate commercial summary suit or conciliation before the Micro and Small Enterprise Facilitation Council (MSEFC).
legal_assessment.realistic_outcome: Clients generally clear genuine dues when threatened with statutory MSME compound interest penalties and blacklisting.
risks_and_caveats: Ensure email proof of client sign-off on delivered milestones exists.
legal_assessment.legal_aid_option: Citizens with annual income below statutory limits (or women) are entitled to free state advocates via DLSA / NALSA.
